findings: ETT.tex:2032-2033 « Since M is globally hyperbolic K is compact » (the recorded finding cites l.2031-2032; the sentence is at l.2032-2033). This is a gap in the argument; the statement is fine. def:globally_hyperbolic gives compact diamonds J(p,q) between two points, and the compactness of K = J⁺(Σ) ∩ J⁻(p) does not follow from them directly. It does hold at every globally hyperbolic, Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifold, for every Cauchy surface Σ and every p, not only p ∈ J⁺(Σ) (Causal.SingularRowsDiamond.isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus). The route is not the paper's. (a) J⁻(W) is open for every open W, from Z⁺ = M and push-up (Causal.Causality.isOpen_Jminus_of_pushUp). (b) J^±(Σ) are closed (lem:Sigma_separe's « In particular », wave 30), and Σ is acausal. (c) A continuous τ strictly increasing along ≤ exists (theo:geroch_sing (i)⇒(ii)). (d) Zorn on time graphs inside the past-noncompact set gives J⁻(p) ∩ Σ compact (Causal.Flat.CBGCompact, no limit curves). (e) Finitely many open diamonds I(a_k, b_k) cover J⁻(p) ∩ Σ, and J⁺(Σ) ∩ J⁻(p) is closed in the union of the compact diamonds J(a_k, p) (CBG.isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus_of_isCompact). Suggest: state the compactness as a lemma before lem:image_diamant, citing (a)-(e) or O'Neill 14.40 for the smooth analogue.

ETT.tex:2036-2037 « it stays above Σ because c(1)=q ∈ K'' lies above i(Σ) and Σ is a Cauchy surface ». The relation σ' ≤ q holds in N, not in M. The step uses M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ) and the acausality of i(Σ) in N: a point of the pulled-back curve in J⁻_M(Σ) is then forced onto Σ. M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ) holds on every T1, second countable space, for any causality and any Cauchy surface: every point lies on an inextensible causal curve, and that curve meets Σ (Causal.Causality.IsCauchySurface.cover_of_t1_secondCountable). So the proof needs neither lem:Sigma_separe (stated later, l.2062) nor its splitting ψ. Suggest: « every point of M lies on an inextensible causal curve, which meets Σ, so M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ); and i(Σ) is acausal in N ». This rewords the recorded finding, whose two inputs are now proved.
questions: No new reading. J_M(Σ, p), with a set as its first argument, is read J⁺_M(Σ) ∩ J⁻_M(p). That extends def:diamonds, which takes two points, and it is Causal.CauchyDiamond's reading. findings: ETT.tex:2058-2059 (recorded, stays). lem:image_diamant is applied to p_n ∈ i(M), but nothing shows i⁻¹(p_n) ∈ J⁺_M(Σ). For a point of J⁻_M(Σ), the diamond J_N(i(Σ), p_n) is {p_n} by acausality of i(Σ). That case is Causal.SingularRowsDiamond.diamond_subset_range, which now holds at every point of M with no Lean hypothesis left.

ETT.tex:2044: neither half of the hypothesis p ∈ ∂ i(M) ∩ J⁺(i(Σ)) is used. The inclusion K⁻_N(p) ∩ J⁺(i(Σ)) ⊂ i(M) and both explicit forms hold for every p in the closure of i(M) (Causal.SingularRowsDiamond.passe_pgcd, passe_pgcd_explicit; already noted in the ledger's notes). The printed form is passe_pgcd_printed. Nothing needs to change. The uses apply it at points of ∂ j₁(N): in lem:corresponding_K (l.2129-2132) at p ∈ ∂ j₁(N) ∩ J⁺(Σ₁), as printed. In prop:Cauchy_point_min (l.2294, 2301) it is applied at the points P_n, P_0 = p for an arbitrary (p,q) ∈ C (l.2276). There p ∈ J⁺(Σ₁) is never stated; it is only implicit in step (B), « c : [0,T*[ → J⁺(Σ₁) with c(0) = P » (l.2280-2281). The closure form needs no such check.

ETT.tex:2059 « The two explicit forms follow from Proposition prop:K_calcul »: true at every E_{>=0}-manifold. The BTZ branch K⁻(p) = J⁻(p) ∖ {p} needs N causal, which N is, being globally hyperbolic (SFABTZ.K_calcul). No change.

kb_proposals: J⁻ of every open set is open under push-up and Z⁺ = M: Causal.Causality.isOpen_Jminus_of_pushUp (model-free, but in a module that imports Causal.Flat.CBG; hoist on demand, kb/0061). Under SingularFlatAxioms it is SingularFlatAxioms.isOpen_Jminus. It discharges hJo of Flat.CBGCompact (T-ett-diamant-rows).

J⁺(Σ) ∩ J⁻(p) is compact for every Cauchy surface Σ and every p of a globally hyperbolic E_{>=0}-manifold: Causal.SingularRowsDiamond.isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus. At the SFA level: SingularFlatAxioms.isCompact_Jplus_inter_Jminus (τ a hypothesis) and _of_modelMeasures. This route uses CBGCompact's Zorn and needs no limit curves. Use it for any named hK or R1 (sigmaCompact) hypothesis of a singular row (T-ett-diamant-rows).

The four CauchyDiamond theorems hold with no named hypothesis at every pair of Hausdorff, second countable E_{>=0}-manifolds: Causal.SingularRowsDiamond.image_diamant, diamond_subset_range, passe_pgcd, passe_pgcd_explicit (Sing = sing₀(N)), and the printed form passe_pgcd_printed. The time-reversed J⁻(Σ) ∩ J⁺(p) is not proved: dualising the openness argument needs Z⁻ = M, which fails at BTZ points (T-ett-diamant-rows).
